analysis.title: Global Asset Allocation Insights, November 2026
key_insights: Fidelity Multi Asset is neutral on equities, credit, government bonds and cash. Credit was upgraded to neutral after modest spread widening. The team says risks are now balanced against strong fundamentals and it is taking a more balanced approach to risk.

The macro backdrop is described as more stagflationary. Growth is moderating from elevated levels while inflation risks persist and bond yields are higher. The team stays cautiously optimistic and would look to add risk on weakness.

Equities: neutral overall. The AI investment cycle still supports earnings, but financing pressures and free cash flow questions are becoming more important. The team closed its Korea and Taiwan trades to reduce exposure to AI-sensitive markets and kept the overweight to emerging markets overall.
Japan is the preferred developed equity market, based on wage-led reflation, resilient earnings and corporate reforms. Emerging markets stay overweight on attractive valuations and strong earnings.

Europe equities face higher energy costs, weaker earnings and tighter ECB policy. UK equities have attractive valuations and defensive traits, but weak earnings momentum and fiscal uncertainty outweigh them. Asia Pacific ex Japan is held back by weak Australian earnings, persistent inflation and a hawkish RBA.
US equities: resilient earnings and improved valuations offset higher real yields and growing concerns over AI financing.

Credit: high yield was raised to overweight on attractive all-in yields and resilient fundamentals, with limited reliance on further spread compression. Investment grade remains underweight (least preferred) because spreads are tight and elevated issuance linked to AI investment is a technical headwind. EM hard currency debt is neutral.

Government bonds are neutral. Higher nominal and real yields improved valuations, but persistent inflation, fiscal pressure and heavy issuance limit a broad rally. Bond-equity correlation is positive, though it has decreased recently, so duration is additive to portfolio risk.

UK Gilts are the preferred developed duration exposure. The team believes markets price a more hawkish Bank of England than is likely. Bunds and JGBs are underweight on fiscal and monetary policy risks. US Treasuries note further Fed tightening as a factor.

Currencies: overweight the US dollar on resilient US growth, a more hawkish Fed, favourable rate differentials and geopolitical uncertainty. Underweight euro (French fiscal uncertainty, energy-related growth risks) and sterling (fiscal concerns). The yen moved to neutral.

Gold remains a positive diversifier on geopolitical and fiscal uncertainty and central-bank demand, though higher yields have moderated conviction. Broad commodities are overweight on tight supply and the risk of further energy disruption.

Watch list: the Iran conflict and energy supply disruption as an inflation risk, AI profitability and financing as focus shifts from capex to cash generation, and whether slowing leading indicators lead to weaker activity and how central banks respond.

Other tactical ideas: Japan mid-caps and banks, European defence, and US transportation with a preference for rail. Options strategies are suggested for downside protection while keeping upside exposure.

sector_views.rationale: Domestic reflation and corporate reform support mid-caps. Banks benefit from monetary policy normalisation and a more favourable rate environment.
Rising procurement budgets and domestic supply chain efforts give a multi-year tailwind, though valuations and near-term sentiment require selectivity.
Tightening supply is improving pricing before demand has fully recovered. Rail has improving volumes and pricing, and positioning is relatively clean after recent weakness.

sector_views.sector: Electrification, grid infrastructure and energy security
sector_views.rationale: Longer-term investment demand continues to support these areas, with increasing focus on earnings visibility and financing resilience.
Resilient cash flows and relative defensiveness if inflation risks persist.

earnings_insights: Corporate earnings are described as strong and growing, supported by the AI investment cycle, which is increasingly benefiting the wider economy. No company-level EPS or revenue figures are given.

The report charts equally weighted 1, 3 and 6 month earnings revisions for Japan, US, Europe, UK, EM and Asia Pacific ex Japan under the heading 'Earnings resilience broadens beyond AI'. The text gives no values.

macro_indicators.interpretation: The report lists further Fed tightening as a factor for US Treasuries and cites a more hawkish Fed as support for the US dollar.

macro_indicators.reading: markets price a more hawkish BoE than is likely to materialise
macro_indicators.interpretation: Supports the team's preference for UK Gilts.
Weighs on European equities and Bunds.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight high yield bonds for income
trade_ideas.rationale: Attractive all-in yields and resilient fundamentals, with limited reliance on spread compression.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight Japanese and emerging market equities
trade_ideas.rationale: Japan has wage-led reflation and corporate reforms. EM has attractive valuations and strong earnings.
trade_ideas.risk: AI financing risks and volatility in AI-sensitive EM markets.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight US dollar, underweight euro and sterling
trade_ideas.rationale: Resilient US growth, favourable rate differentials and geopolitical uncertainty support the dollar. French fiscal and energy-related growth risks weigh on the euro, and fiscal concerns on sterling.

trade_ideas.description: Overweight UK Gilts, underweight Bunds and JGBs
trade_ideas.rationale: Gilts offer attractive relative value and the market is pricing a more hawkish BoE than likely. Bunds and JGBs face fiscal and monetary policy risks.

trade_ideas.description: Hold gold and overweight broad commodities
trade_ideas.rationale: Gold is supported by central-bank demand and geopolitical and fiscal uncertainty. Commodities are supported by tight supply and energy disruption risk.
trade_ideas.risk: Higher yields have moderated conviction in gold.

trade_ideas.description: Options strategies for downside protection while retaining upside
trade_ideas.rationale: Strong fundamentals are balanced by elevated risks and traditional diversification is less reliable.
Tightening supply is improving pricing ahead of a demand recovery, and positioning is clean.
Domestic reflation and corporate reform support mid-caps, and banks benefit from policy normalisation.

risk_factors: Iran conflict escalation or energy supply disruption renewing inflation pressure.
AI financing and profitability concerns, including free cash flow and funding sustainability.
Slowing leading indicators translating into weaker activity.
Persistent inflation and higher bond yields.
Fiscal pressures and heavy government bond issuance.
French fiscal uncertainty and sovereign spread volatility in euro government bonds.
charts_described: Chart titled 'Earnings resilience broadens beyond AI' plots equally weighted 1, 3 and 6M earnings revisions for Japan, US, Europe, UK, EM and Asia Pacific ex Japan from Jan-25 to Oct-26. The text gives no values.

Chart titled 'High yield more attractive as yields rise and spreads widen' shows yield and spread percentiles since 2006 for global, EUR, US, Asia, Latam, EM corporate and UK high yield, this month versus last month. The text gives no values.

Chart titled 'Government bonds driven by oil prices this year' shows the rolling 60-day correlation of 10-year yields and oil for the US, Germany, UK, Japan, Canada and Australia. The text gives no values.
vol_and_positioning: Options strategies are recommended for targeted downside protection while keeping exposure to upside, given strong fundamentals balanced by elevated risks and less reliable traditional diversification.
US transportation positioning is described as relatively clean after recent weakness.
The report notes that closing the Korea and Taiwan trades followed rising financing risks and volatility in AI-sensitive markets.
geopolitical: Iran conflict: further escalation or disruption to energy supplies could renew inflation pressure and prolong a stagflationary environment.
Geopolitical fragmentation is cited as supporting higher defence spending in Europe.
French fiscal uncertainty is cited as a negative for the euro and euro government bonds.

key_data_points.metric: Typical time horizon of the views
key_data_points.context: The views are a broad starting point for asset allocation and do not reflect current positions for investment strategies.
key_data_points.anchor: Views reflect a typical time horizon of 12–18 months and provide a broad starting point for asset allocation decisions.

tension_points.bull_case: Strong corporate earnings and the AI investment cycle continue to support growth and are increasingly benefiting the wider economy.
tension_points.bear_case: Financing pressures and free cash flow questions around AI capex are becoming more important, and elevated AI-linked bond issuance is a headwind for investment grade credit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The team would look to add risk on weakness if the outlook improves. It flags a shift in focus from capex commitments to cash generation, profitability and funding sustainability as the risk to watch.

tension_points.bull_case: Higher nominal and real yields have improved valuations, particularly if growth continues to moderate.
tension_points.bear_case: Persistent inflation, fiscal pressures and heavy issuance limit a broad rally, and positive equity-bond correlation reduces diversification.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A more sustained decline in inflation or a meaningful growth slowdown would improve the outlook for government bonds.

theme_stances.key_argument: Financing risks and volatility in AI-sensitive markets led the team to close Korea and Taiwan trades.
theme_stances.evidence: closing our Korea and Taiwan trades while retaining an overweight to emerging markets

theme_stances.key_argument: Attractive all-in yields and strong fundamentals make high yield a source of carry.
Resilient US growth, favourable rate differentials and geopolitical uncertainty support the dollar.
theme_stances.evidence: We remain overweight the US dollar
